description: The fatal READ arm of 1000-ACCTFILE-GET-NEXT at app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L92-L116 reached with MORE THAN ONE row stored, which is the one property no other case in this directory asserts: that the browse STOPS at the first refused read instead of reporting it and carrying on. case13 and case14 pin the same arm with a single stored row, and a single row cannot see that difference - a translation that logged the refusal and continued the browse would reach end of file on its very next read, set END-OF-FILE at L108, close cleanly and emit the closing banner, and against one stored row the only visible symptom is the extra banner. Against three it is unmistakable: a browse that continued would emit three error triples, or the remaining rows as records, or both. What the case declares: three ACCTFILE rows, so the dataset is there and 0000-ACCTFILE-OPEN succeeds at L136 with '00' - this case is about the READ and not the OPEN - and the first READ at L93 then reports a permanent error, because no stored row is a CVACT01Y record. Each measures 122 bytes where app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy declares 300, and 122 is not arbitrary: it is the sum of the twelve named spans (11 + 1 + 12 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10 + 10 + 12 + 12 + 10 + 10), the account record with its trailing FILLER PIC X(178) span absent, 300 - 178. The twelve spans sit at offsets 0, 11, 12, 24, 36, 48, 58, 68, 78, 90, 102 and 112 and the FILLER at 122, and those offsets are read off the copybook mechanically rather than from prose, which is what makes the width a derivation and not an assertion of taste. From ACCT-ACTIVE-STATUS onward each row is a row of app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt verbatim - rows 0, 1 and 2 respectively - including the three '{' zoned sign overpunches that close the S9(10)V99 spans at offsets 13, 25 and 37, where '{' encodes a positive digit zero; ACCT-ADDR-ZIP at offset 102 carries 'A000000000' and ACCT-GROUP-ID at offset 112 is ten spaces, and the copybook's misspelled ACCT-EXPIRAION-DATE at offset 58 is preserved as it is spelt rather than corrected. Only ACCT-ID is changed, to 00000000601, 00000000602 and 00000000603, identifiers no row of that fixture carries, so no row here can be mistaken for one of the fifty stored records. The rows are seeded in DESCENDING key order, as case20 does on the successful path, because a KSDS browse reads in key order whatever order the records were loaded in: app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl:L29-L33 declares ACCTFILE as ORGANIZATION INDEXED, ACCESS MODE SEQUENTIAL, RECORD KEY FD-ACCT-ID, so the row the first READ reaches is 00000000601 and not the row inserted first. That row is byte-identical to case13's single row, deliberately: the two cases then differ in exactly two variables - the row count and the insertion order - and the fingerprint they share is the evidence that neither of those changes what the arm does. The ladder at L94-L103 is evaluated in source order and only its third arm is taken. L94 IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '00' would MOVE 0 TO APPL-RESULT and PERFORM 1100-DISPLAY-ACCT-RECORD: not taken. L98 ELSE IF ACCTFILE-STATUS = '10' would MOVE 16 TO APPL-RESULT, satisfying the 88 APPL-EOF condition declared at L63 and ending the loop silently through L108: not taken, because the status reported is not '10'. L100-L101 ELSE MOVE 12 TO APPL-RESULT: taken. The guard chain then fails twice - 88 APPL-AOK at L104 is false because APPL-RESULT is 12 and not 0, and 88 APPL-EOF at L107 is false because it is 12 and not 16 - so L109-L113 run in order: DISPLAY 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at L110, MOVE ACCTFILE-STATUS TO IO-STATUS at L111, PERFORM 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS at L112 which emits the status line, and PERFORM 9999-ABEND-PROGRAM at L113 which displays 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L170, moves 0 into TIMING at L171 and 999 into ABCODE at L172, and calls 'CEE3ABD' at L173. The return code is therefore 12, from the MOVE 12 at L101 and carried out by that call; it is never 16, which is the APPL-EOF value, never 0, never 8, and never 999 - ABCODE 999 at L172 and TIMING 0 at L171 are Language Environment abend parameters and are not the return code. The closing banner at L85 is ABSENT even though the OPEN succeeded and the program was one statement from reaching it, because L173 terminates the run: 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE at L83 is never performed, no 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' line can appear, and a translation that emitted the L85 banner from a finally block would fail here. Nothing is displayed before the failure either - the first READ never yielded a decodable record, so no labelled field line, no 49-dash separator and no 300-byte record image appears anywhere - so SYSOUT is exactly these four lines, of 38, 26, 24 and 16 characters. WHAT THIS CASE DOES NOT PIN, STATED RATHER THAN IMPLIED: the fatal arm of 9000-ACCTFILE-CLOSE at L151-L167 is not reachable from any parity case of this program, and this case does not pretend to reach it. That arm needs the dataset to stop being addressable BETWEEN the browse and the close, which is a temporal condition no seeded dataset expresses: a BATCH_JOB case may declare only its datasets and its JCL PARM values - ParityCase refuses it a screenRequest, and with it the forced outcomes an online case can declare, and app/jcl/READACCT.jcl declares no PARM, so inventing a job parameter to carry an instruction would misstate that JCL contract - and a seed of uniform width either decodes at every read or fails at the first, because ParityHarness refuses a ragged dataset. The arm is asserted where it can be driven: AccountBalanceJobTest.closeFailsForEveryNonZeroStatus scripts a failing CLOSE over a complete pass and requires the opening banner, the record's thirteen lines, 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' at L162, the rendered status at L164 and 'ABENDING PROGRAM' at L170, requires that the closing banner is absent, and requires return code 12 - which is the same 12 this case states, because the close paragraph's ADD 8 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at L152, SUBTRACT APPL-RESULT FROM APPL-RESULT at L155 and ADD 12 TO ZERO GIVING APPL-RESULT at L157 are an idiom peculiar to that paragraph, preserved rather than normalised, whose values are nonetheless identical to the plain MOVE 8, MOVE 0 and MOVE 12 the open and read paragraphs use. Deriving the status line, step by step from the renderer: 01 IO-STATUS-04 is IO-STATUS-0401 PIC 9 followed by IO-STATUS-0403 PIC 999 at L57-L59, four bytes in total, and both arms of 9910-DISPLAY-IO-STATUS display the 20-character literal 'FILE STATUS IS: NNNN' followed by that image, so the line is 24 characters and the NNNN is part of the hard-coded literal at L183 and L187 rather than a placeholder awaiting substitution. The numeric ELSE arm at L184-L187 is taken when IO-STATUS is numeric and IO-STAT1 is not '9': MOVE '0000' TO IO-STATUS-04, then MOVE IO-STATUS TO IO-STATUS-04(3:2), which overlays the third and fourth bytes only - a status of '42' would render 0, 0, 4, 2 and give FILE STATUS IS: NNNN0042. That arm is unreachable from this suite. The IF arm at L177-L183 is taken instead when IO-STATUS is not numeric or IO-STAT1 is '9': it moves IO-STAT1 into IO-STATUS-04(1:1) and the binary value of IO-STAT2 into IO-STATUS-0403. This translation reaches its data through a configuration-bound JDBC driver whose refusal carries no VSAM feedback code to report, so AccountRepository reports PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS - '9' followed by a binary-zero feedback byte - for a row whose width it will not decode fields from, and that status takes the IF arm, renders 9 then 000, and gives FILE STATUS IS: NNNN9000, also 24 characters. The frozen contract fixes that value rather than leaving it to a case: CBACT01CParityTest requires every case whose return code is not zero to end with the rendering composed from AccountRepository.PERMANENT_ERROR_STATUS followed by 'ABENDING PROGRAM', and to carry as its third-from-last line one of the two error literals a case of this program can reach. This case therefore states 9000 and the divergence from a mainframe permanent I/O error's 0030 is recorded here rather than silently resolved, exactly as case10 records the open arm's 0035 and case13 the read arm's 0030. What the branch it pins does not depend on is that four-character image: the arm reached, the literal displayed, the guard chain that fails twice, the absent closing banner and the return code 12 are all identical either way. The program's three error literals are deliberately inconsistent and are reproduced exactly rather than harmonised: the read literal at L110 is 'ERROR READING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26 characters, the open literal at L144 is the bare DD name in 'ERROR OPENING ACCTFILE' at 22, and the close literal at L162 is 'ERROR CLOSING ACCOUNT FILE' at 26. Nothing is written anywhere, and "expectedWrites" being empty asserts that positively rather than expressing a lack of interest. No final state is reported for ACCTFILE and none is expected: a 122-byte row has no 300-byte layout to be described by, and describing it under one would be a false statement about its bytes rather than an assertion about them. The case is deterministic: the condition it forces is a fixed literal row width, and it carries no wall-clock value and no random value. It declares no job parameter, because app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L22 is a bare EXEC PGM=CBACT01C with no PARM. The dataset is addressed only by its binding key, ACCTFILE, which is the DD name at app/jcl/READACCT.jcl:L25; no fully-qualified dataset name appears here, because those live only in application.yml. Every line and every byte of every seeded row is US-ASCII, the code page of app/data/ASCII and of ParityHarness.FIXTURE_CHARSET, and never a platform default. Provenance: statically derived by reading app/cbl/CBACT01C.cbl, app/cpy/CVACT01Y.cpy, app/jcl/READACCT.jcl and app/data/ASCII/acctdata.txt, cross-checked against the constants published by AccountBalanceJob, AbendException, AccountRepository and FileStatus. Nothing here was captured from, recorded against or replayed from a run of the legacy COBOL, which is empirically impossible in this environment - there is no z/OS runtime, the available compiler reports its indexed file handler as disabled, and no Language Environment CEE service exists to link the CALL 'CEE3ABD' at L173 - and that substitution of provenance, and nothing else about the gate, is the escalated deviation recorded as risk R-A.
